content_html:
Chocolate combines fat, sugar, cocoa, and sometimes milk, so a stain may need more than a quick rinse. The practical approach is to remove excess without spreading it, work with cool water, and make sure the mark is gone before using dryer or iron heat.

Lift off excess chocolate without rubbing it in

If the chocolate is solid, lift it with a spoon or dull edge. If it is soft, remove as much as possible from the outside toward the center so the stained area does not spread.

Rinse from the back with cool or lukewarm water

Hold the back of the stained area under water so residue is pushed out of the fabric. Avoid starting with very hot water, which can make stains containing milk or protein harder to remove.

Pretreat with a compatible laundry detergent

Apply a small amount of liquid detergent or stain remover that is safe for the garment and follow the label contact time. On delicate fabrics, test first in an inconspicuous area.

Check the stain before drying

Wash according to the care label and inspect the area in good light before using the dryer. If a shadow remains, repeat pretreatment; heat can set residue that another wash might otherwise remove.
